visual_source_files.evidence: README.md embeds assets/intro.png; the 2632×838 RGBA image matches p. 2 Figure 1 overview (query card, Traditional ERM/Ours panels, cue checklist and Answer: Angry). It is a rendered PNG, not an editable generator.
Public pipeline code exposes the speaker/prosody/stress/intonation fields used by Figure 2 and Appendix prompts; it supports method semantics only and is not a Figure/Table layout source.
Public DSP implementation documents pitch, energy, speaking rate and contour measurements referenced by Figure 2; no plotting or table-generation code is present.
Public augmentation code supports the GPT-4o prompt semantics in Figure 5, but does not generate the PDF prompt card or any chart/table.

source_acquisition.search_note: PDF homepage/project link and OpenReview forum were checked, followed by gh repo metadata and recursive tree inspection. The author repository exactly matches the paper title and contains one matching overview render (assets/intro.png) plus method/prompt-support code, but no plot*, figure*, table*, TeX/TikZ/PGF, SVG, notebook, or editable Figure 2–9/Table 1–8 source. The inventory CSV had classified the repository as repository_without_visual_source because no compact visual file was registered; direct inspection justifies partial_visual_source for Figure 1 only. assets/EmotionThinker.png is a second overview-family render without a documented one-to-one PDF-figure mapping.

paper_style.palette_strategy: Figures 1–3 use pastel blue/cream/lilac/green/yellow cards with dark outlines for method roles; Figure 4 uses blue cards with red/green text highlights; Table 1 uses red crosses/green checks, Tables 2–7 use monochrome rules with bold/underline and a shaded ours row, and Appendix Figures 5–9/Table 8 are grayscale prompt/text objects.
paper_style.vector_raster_mix: Body, captions, equations, table text and rules are PDF vector objects. Figure 1 has a matching author PNG render; Figures 2–4 mix embedded cards/icons with PDF text, while Figures 5–9 are gray prompt-card compositions with embedded Aptos text. Table 8 is vector long-form text with rules. No public editable chart/diagram/table generator was found.
paper_style.style_consistency: Nimbus Roman and Computer Modern remain stable for publication text and tables, with consistent Figure/Table caption syntax and booktabs-like table rules. Handwritten pastel diagrams, red/green qualitative cards and Aptos grayscale prompt cards form separate local subsystems rather than one global visual language.

cross_object_system.visual_narrative: Figure 1 establishes the classification-to-explanation interface; Figure 2 gives the EmotionCoT-35K data pipeline and Table 1 quantifies feature coverage; Figure 3 supplies GRPO-PTR architecture; Table 5 tests prosody as a prerequisite; Table 2/3 report overall and human results; Figure 4 and Table 8 show grounding/failure cases; Table 4/6/7 close component, K and reward-weight ablations; Figures 5–9 preserve prompt and evaluator details in the appendix.
cross_object_system.caption_system: Figures 1–4 mostly use title plus comparison/encoding, with Figure 3 naming upper/lower regions and Figure 4 defining red/green highlights. Figures 5–9 captions only name prompt templates and parts, with little self-contained setup or finding. Table 2 has the strongest unit/metric/top-two explanation; Tables 3/6/7 are terse; Table 8 states a finding but overclaims the number of representative models.
cross_object_system.table_header_system: Table 1 uses Dataset/Reasoning plus a two-level Acoustic Feature block; Table 2 uses two metric blocks; Table 4 uses Variations/Training Strategy plus SER/ER; Tables 3 and 5–7 use compact single-level headers; Table 8 uses Model/Reasoning for long text. Black/white rules are stable while narrow-table abbreviations and units depend on nearby prose.
cross_object_system.method_result_ablation_link: Figure 2/Table 1 → prosody SFT → Table 5 → Figure 3 GRPO-PTR → Table 2 main comparison; Table 4 removes RM/trust/progressive components, Table 6 changes K and Table 7 changes reward weights, while Figure 4/Table 8 supply qualitative grounding. The chain supports the paper narrative but lacks seeds, cost columns, denominators and aggregate error rates.
cross_object_system.main_appendix_link: Section 3.1 points to Figure 2 and Appendix B; Section 3.2 points to Table 5 and Appendix C; Sections 3.3/4.2 point to Figures 3/4 and Appendices D–F. Figure 5 is B.3, Figures 6/7 are D.2, Figures 8/9 are E, and Table 8 is F. Appendix adds prompts and long outputs but no editable visual source.
cross_object_system.typography_consistency: Publication text/table typography is consistently Nimbus Roman with Computer Modern math; Figure 1–4 diagrams introduce ChalkboardSE and Figure 5–9 prompt cards use Aptos. The distinction is legible as modular but not globally unified.
cross_object_system.color_consistency: Main diagrams reuse pale blue/cream/lilac/green role colors and dark outlines, while Tables and appendix prompt cards intentionally stay grayscale. Red/green cue highlights in Figure 4 and checks/crosses in Table 1 provide semantics but are not robust to grayscale/color-vision limitations.

most_reusable_patterns: Figure 1 same-input dual cards make categorical output versus cue-grounded reasoning legible in one headline canvas.
Figure 2 data→features→reasoning LLM→labeled example and Figure 3 rollout→reward decomposition form a useful paired data/method interface.
Table 2 grouped headers, Table 4 baseline-to-component rows and Figure 4/Table 8 same-input qualitative cards connect headline, mechanism and failure evidence.
Gray prompt cards can preserve reproducibility details, but Part 1/2 captions should state the pairing and field names should be consistent.
highest_value_objects: Figure 1 for problem/method interface and headline contrast.
Figure 3 for the GRPO-PTR reward/trust/progressive mechanism.
Table 2 for the central accuracy-plus-reasoning comparison.
Table 4 and Table 5 for component ablation and prosody prerequisite.
Figure 4 for a concrete grounding/failure contrast; Table 8 is a useful but single-case appendix expansion.
failure_patterns: Small text and high information density in diagrams, qualitative cards and the four-page long table.
Pastel and red/green encodings are not grayscale/color-vision safe despite some textual redundancy.
Tables 2/4/5/6/7 and Table 8 omit seeds, intervals or denominators; K efficiency is discussed without actual cost.
Table 8 caption model count conflicts with visible rows, and Figures 5–9 expose prompt spelling/count inconsistencies that weaken machine reproduction.
final_judgment.one_sentence_visual_strategy: Use classification→cue-grounded reasoning→prosody SFT→progressive trust-aware RL→overall/ablation/case as the visual spine, with pastel architecture and grouped result tables for method/performance and grayscale prompt cards/longtable for reproducibility boundaries; the public repository supplies only a matching Figure 1 render.
